metal_inputs.BaseColor: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: flat seamless PBR BaseColor texture, sRGB albedo only, a 120 x 120 mm material sample for the vertical steel leg tubes of this old classroom desk. Image 1 is the primary real-desk reference: inspect specifically the two LOWER photos, the VERTICAL leg tubes have widespread irregular mottled small paint loss, grey-brown oxidized steel flecks and short scratch chips over their entire visible height. Image 2 is the current companion horizontal-brace albedo: preserve its pale neutral cool grey paint and grey-brown bare metal palette, but CHANGE ONLY wear distribution to match the aged VERTICAL tubes. Create a square, straight-on flat material swatch filling the frame, not a cylinder or furniture render. Retain roughly 70-78% pale grey painted enamel, with 22-30% exposed dark grey and muted grey-brown steel/oxidation in many irregular densely scattered 0.3-3 mm chipped spots and smaller pin pits, some connected 2-6 mm clusters and fine short scuff lines. Patch density softly varies on 15-35 mm areas but all quadrants look equally old, not a clean half. Oxide flecks are darker than the paint, with tiny subdued bare-steel grey cores, soft 0.1-0.3 mm paint-edge breaks. Thin enamel, realistic used school-desk legs from the lower reference. Mostly mottled and isotropic with short vertical scratches; no long continuous polished corridor, no broad rust cloud, no rings, no large peeling scales. Seamless edge-to-edge for repeat. Albedo only: completely uniform flat illumination, no reflections, shadows, highlights, perspective, labels, borders, logo, grid, or watermark. Production texture with restrained realistic fine detail. Whole square is the material, no desk background.
metal_inputs.Metallic: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: the supplied square BaseColor material swatch of aged classroom-desk vertical tubes. Change ONLY its pixel values into a registered grayscale PBR Metallic data map. Preserve every existing chipped patch, thin rim, pin pit and short scratch at exactly the same pixel footprint and preserve square crop and seamless repeat. Solid enamel is PURE BLACK (0), the exact grey-brown exposed flecks predominantly neutral mid-grey 0.35-0.50 for oxidized steel, with smaller subtly brighter 0.75-0.90 steel cores. Thin brown corrosion at their edges 0.10-0.25. Sharp but antialiased tiny paint breaks. All enamel grey fabric micrograin becomes black: it is nonmetal. No new patches, no changed density, no geometry, no perspective, no shadows, no albedo, no text. Whole image grayscale encoded scalar map; registered to the input without changing layout.
metal_inputs.Roughness: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: supplied aged-desk vertical-tube BaseColor swatch. Convert ONLY pixel colors to the registered grayscale PBR Roughness channel, preserving the precise chip/rim/pit/scratch positions, scale, crop and seamless square repeat. Matte worn grey enamel about 0.50 with fine subtle 0.47-0.57 grain and slight age variation; oxidized grey-brown spots 0.58-0.76; small exposed steel cores 0.34-0.45; tiny scratched exposed marks about 0.38-0.48. Darker is smoother, white rougher. This vertical tube is weathered mottled metal, it has no large polished stripe. Absolutely no new patches, no painted-colour interpretation, no lighting or shadows, no normals, no labels, no furniture. Scalar grayscale value map registered to input.
metal_inputs.Height: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: supplied aged-desk vertical-tube BaseColor texture. Change ONLY pixel values into a precisely registered grayscale PBR Height map, keeping exact existing spot boundaries, pin pits, short scuffs, seamless square crop and pattern position. Thin paint surface is midgrey 0.557 with very subtle fine enamel grain +/-0.007. Missing paint patches are slightly lower 0.44-0.49; brown oxide fine pits inside them 0.38-0.45, tiny residual paint rims about 0.56, no tall bubbly flakes. Use a shallow realistic enamel step, microscopic pits and thin scratched depressions. Do NOT add huge contrast, mountain relief, new crack patterns, large peeling scales, a rub corridor, object shading, cast shadows, lettering, or furniture. Flat scalar grayscale height channel exactly registered to the supplied albedo.

prompts.BaseColor: Create one seamless square physically based BASE COLOR texture, straight flat scan with absolutely no light, no shadows, no specular shading, no AO, no perspective, no object, no text. Material: aged charcoal-black molded rubber feet on an old school desk; consistent with dark almost black cylindrical foot caps in the supplied photographic reference. Patch covers 80 x 80 millimetres in real life. Dominant subdued charcoal rubber RGB around 35,38,40; mildly rubbed smoother areas with subtle grey wispy shoe and floor scuffs; sparse extremely fine shallow abrasion lines 0.05–0.2 mm wide and small grey-brown dust traces, leaving most surface dark. Gentle large-scale variation but no cloudy stone texture, no craters, no granular rock, no rust, no metallic highlights, no white chips. Rubbed scuffs around 12% coverage, low contrast. Manufactured fine matte rubber grain, really tiny. Seamless left-right top-bottom. Only the single base-color material swatch filling the entire square.
prompts.Roughness: Edit this BASE COLOR rubber texture into a registered single-channel grayscale ROUGHNESS map for exactly the same pixel positions. Single flat square seamless data image, no illumination. Rubber roughness gray level 155/255 for normal dark intact fine-grain rubber, smoother rubbed wispy abrasion bands and narrow scuff lines around 110-130/255, small dusty specks around185/255; restrained subtle finegrain variation plus or minus 6 levels. Keep all positions, widths and silhouettes of marks locked to the supplied image. All roughness stays in range100–205, no black or white. No new marks, no decorative shading, no borders or text. Very low contrast fine rubber finish, never rock. RGB channels identical.
prompts.Height: Convert the supplied charcoal rubber base-color texture to a precisely registered linear grayscale HEIGHT data map. Keep exactly the same square framing and locations of all wispy rubbing and shallow scuff lines. Rubber is smooth, base level 128/255, fine tiny manufactured grain only +-1 to 2 grayscale values. Shallow abrasion lines are 123–126/255, broad rubbed wisps vary only127–128, a very few dust specks129. Absolutely no color, no shadows, no relief illumination, no new details, no thick gouges, no rock or sponge texture, no visible depth exaggeration, no text or border. Pixels stay close to neutral mid-gray; it describes micrometre-scale rubber skin, not thick damage. Seamless grayscale single channel image filling the square.
